In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reactivity of the blood vessels of chronic experimental hypertensive animals is not affected by prolonged antihyptensive therapy.
the reactivity of the mesenteric arteries in chronic experimental hypertensive animals is enhanced due to adaptive/structural changes which cannot be reversed by long‐term antihypertension therapy.

the increased reactivity to vasoconstrictors of the mesenteric arteries from the chronic hypertensive rat is due to adaptive/structural changes and not due to a change in the functional characteristics of the vascular smooth muscle cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increased reactivity of blood vessels in chronic experimental hypertensive animals is a result of adaptive/structural changes and that the changes in the vascular wall cannot be reversed by long‐term antihypertenisve therapy.
the reactivity of the blood vessels is not affected by the blood pressure, but by the duration of the elevated blood pressure.
the hyperreactivity of the blood vessels of hypertensive animals is a result of a combination of the increased blood pressure and the adaptive/structural alterations in the vessels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hyperresponsivenss of blood vessels to vasoconstrictors in chronic experimental hypertension is a secondary phenomenon and that the structural changes in the blood vessel wall cannot be reversed by antihypertensives.

the increased reactivity of the blood vessels of hypertensive rats is not reversed by long‐term antihypertensives and that the adaptive changes in the vessels of hypertensives are not reversed by long term antihypertension.
